A full-fidelity desktop website design comp, 16:9 landscape, showing the top of the page at 1440 px wide, rendered edge to edge as the page itself (no browser window, no device, no desk). The website for PrismTTY, a live terminal-output highlighter for network engineers. The whole page is built as an IETF RFC plain-text document on a near-black ground (#0d0e0d), set entirely in ONE size of a crisp modern slab-serif monospace (a refined Courier-like face) in warm light gray (#d6d8d0), with dim gray (#6f7369) for secondary text. Hierarchy comes only from capitals, numbering, rules drawn with characters, and one reversed line. No bold display type, no gradients, no glow, no cards, no rounded boxes, no icons.

Regions, top to bottom:
1. RFC header block across the top in two columns of monospace text. Left: "Independent Submission", "Request for Comments: PrismTTY", "Category: Informational". Right, right-aligned: "inxbit", "October 2026", and two underlined links "GitHub" and "crates.io". A small prism-triangle logo glyph (an outlined triangle with a tiny terminal window inside) sits just before the first line, in the same gray.
2. A centered title line in capitals: "READABLE OUTPUT, LIVE IN YOUR TERMINAL".
3. "Abstract" at the left margin, then an indented paragraph: "PrismTTY wraps your shell, SSH sessions, pipes and logs and colors the output already flowing through your terminal, with built-in profiles for Cisco, Juniper, Fortinet, Palo Alto, Arista, Aruba CX, Versa and Linux. It never logs in to devices and stores nothing by default."
4. The primary action: one reversed line (a light gray bar with dark text) reading "$ brew install inxbit/tap/prismtty" with a bracketed "[ Copy ]" control at its right end, and below it in dim gray "or   cargo install prismtty".
5. A left column "Table of Contents" with dot leaders: "1.  Introduction ........ 1", "2.  Profiles ............ 2", "3.  Profile Switching ... 3", "4.  Installation ........ 4", "5.  Scope ............... 5".
6. Filling the right two-thirds, the dominant element: "Figure 1: the same output, raw and through PrismTTY", an exhibit framed with + - | characters holding two stacked copies of one Cisco session. The top copy is entirely gray: "LAB-IOS-01#show interfaces description", a table header "Interface  Status  Protocol  Description", rows "Gi1/0/1  up  up  Uplink to LAB-CORE", "Gi1/0/2  down  down  Spare access port", "Po10  up  up  Bundle to DIST-A", "Vlan1191  up  up  Synthetic users VLAN", then "LAB-IOS-01#show ip route" and "O  192.0.2.0/24 [110/20] via 198.51.100.1, 00:00:14, Vlan1191". The bottom copy is the identical text highlighted exactly like a real terminal: the prompt "LAB-IOS-01#" pure white, interface names Gi1/0/1, Gi1/0/2, Po10, Vlan1191 in bright blue #0099ff, every "up" in pure green #00ff00, "down" in bold pure red #ff0000, IP addresses in cyan #00ffff. These saturated terminal colors are the ONLY color anywhere on the page. A small bracketed toggle sits above the figure: "[ raw | PrismTTY ]".
7. At the bottom edge, the start of the next section: "1.  Introduction" at the left margin with the first line of a paragraph, and an RFC page footer line "inxbit                 Informational                 [Page 1]".

Generous margins, strict 72-column feel, everything aligned to one monospace character grid. Dark, calm and exacting, like reading RFC 791 in a dark room at 2 a.m. during a change window. Real readable text at real size, about 16 px on a 1440 px page.
